source.title: Learning-Time Encoding Shapes Unlearning in LLMs
source.authors: Rui-Han Wu; Konstantin Garov; Kamalika Chaudhuri

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how fine-tuning encodings and text structure change the effectiveness of GA and task-vector unlearning. Its results qualify claims about unlearning effectiveness, but it does not test the listed recovery attacks directly.
record.gate_note: The extraction trade-off evaluates unlearned models using unseen paraphrased descriptions, but reports aggregate trade-off metrics rather than a standalone rephrasing attack against a fixed near-chance checkpoint. The paper mentions Who's Harry Potter and other methods in related work but reports no results for them. No fine-tuning recovery attack, activation-direction ablation, or quantization attack is tested.
record.test_reason: The study compares how training-time encoding changes the forget-versus-retain trade-off of GA and task-vector unlearning, using Norm-AUC curves over checkpoints. It reports no checkpoint at near-chance targeted accuracy and no general ability after unlearning. It runs no attack on an unlearned model: no relearning, no activation edits, no quantization, and no prompting attack. The unseen-paraphrase 'extraction trade-off' is its standard evaluation probe, not a recovery attack on a checkpoint that looks unlearned. Its construct is how selective unlearning is, and how that depends on fine-tuning data structure. That is related to whether unlearning is shallow, but it is a different construct, so it bears on none of versions A–F.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that learning-time knowledge encoding shapes post-hoc unlearning. Fine-tuning on multiple paraphrases improves the forget/retain trade-off (44/48 extraction, 39/48 memorization comparisons). Unlearning single facts entangled with retained content in text chunks is largely non-selective (Norm-AUC near 0.5). Aligning splits to chunks, or isolating facts, helps. They recommend 'paraphrasing' and 'separating' as training-time strategies. They note the results cover fine-tuned models only; extension to pretraining is left to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Tests GA and task-vector unlearning on controlled fictional knowledge fine-tuning datasets; it does not reproduce the original sources' methods or test their recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with fine-tuning representation, whether target and retain facts share text chunks, alignment of the unlearn split to chunk boundaries, dataset, model, algorithm, and unlearning-data encoding.

fits_no_version.finding: With entangled text chunks (Eval-DU+ FT-Mul-Chunk), GA and TV Norm-AUC sits near 0.5 (0.45–0.61): target and retained knowledge are removed at similar rates. Aligning the unlearn split to chunk boundaries or isolating facts within chunks raises Norm-AUC by +0.02 to +0.14. Paraphrased fine-tuning (FT-Mul) matches or beats FT-Single in 44/48 comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How knowledge was encoded at training time (paraphrase diversity, whether forget and retain facts are entangled within chunks) determines how selectively post-hoc unlearning can remove it.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to fine-tuned models and synthetic fictional facts. The authors defer validation on pretrained models. The reported Norm-AUC values are trade-off summaries, not direct post-attack recovery rates or targeted accuracy at a specified near-chance point; no post-unlearning general-capability results are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3's individual FT-Single/FT-Mul configurations are not itemized; the paper's reported aggregate count (44 out of 48) is retained in r55. Table 8 memorization-trade-off values, figures, and fine-tuning general-benchmark results are omitted because they do not directly add separate results on the recovery attacks in the claim.

untested.parts: No near-chance targeted accuracy at a chosen checkpoint, no post-unlearning general-capability benchmark (Table 7 covers fine-tuning only), and no attack on the unlearned models.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.

Unseen paraphrases serve only as the evaluation probe across the whole trade-off curve. There is no comparison of rephrased versus original prompts on a fixed unlearned checkpoint, and no jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context attacks.
No method is claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests A / T5' and 'partial' states are reclassified. A Norm-AUC trade-off summary cannot show near-chance forgetting, preserved general ability, or resistance to recovery. The original sources (WHP, WMDP, Eight Methods) appear only in related work. The experiments use synthetic fictional facts and fine-tuned models only.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests forgetting-versus-retention trade-offs for GA and task vector. It does not establish targeted accuracy near chance, measure general ability after unlearning, or directly test recovery attacks.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis showing that unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
Unseen paraphrased descriptions are used to evaluate extraction trade-offs, but the study does not isolate prompting-only recovery as an attack or compare it with a never-trained control.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

rows.subject: Llama2-7B, Eval-DU+ (FT-Mul-Chunk)

conditions.value: original; target and retain facts may share chunks

rows.note: Authors describe most Eval-DU+ values near 0.5 as indicating limited selective-unlearning effectiveness.
rows.check: Norm-AUC is a relative forget-vs-retain efficiency summary from Table 4. It is not targeted accuracy near chance, general ability, or recovery after an attack. Norm-AUC near 0.5 means forget and retain scores fall at the same rate, which says nothing about hidden knowledge being recoverable. The 'partial' state against A is unfounded.
